how: Calls recruit members to build, fix, and defend named work at coordinates.
Mobilization fluctuates with a streamer's availability and audience attention rather than depending only on a persistent room call.

statement: Seeking the streamer's attention as a reason to place
how: An audience member explains placement as seeking Tyler's attention, preserving a stated motive beyond recruitment for the mark without treating it as verified for all viewers.
Insufficient offline defenders make non-infringing space and a larger ally attractive alternatives.
An attack challenge receives a bare commitment, while portrait work also receives a short report of one pixel placed.
An unanswered mark proposal and a portrait proposer reporting initial work show distinct forms of starting without establishing one continuous founder-led project.
Representation takes the form of streamer faces, ALPHA, and the room's short 12 BTW joke.
Members report the portrait's starting coordinates, an outlined chin, and later completion of the sign.
Coordinate requests and a mandatory shared coordinate align placement without demonstrating that design disagreement was settled.
Members copy, test, update, and keep placement scripts running.
Automation requires changing target versions and reverting from an expanded portrait script to a smaller repair target.
One room cannot test the comparative prevalence claim, and leader language cannot decide whether formal order was appointed or absent.
Tyler's relayed wishes and audience draw shape objectives without establishing formal appointment, enforceable command, or universal compliance.
Completion leads explicitly to maintenance, defence calls, overnight coverage, and concentration on the smaller portrait target.
Members attribute attacks and flag restoration to named groups without independent verification of individual placements.
A member reports negotiating peace and mutual defence with a neighbouring group.
A self-reported negotiator carries a peace proposal without demonstrated authority over every placer.
Members offer reciprocal repair after their own mark is restored, while another group offers attack assistance in exchange for building space.
A member reports an ongoing joint raid with another streamer community rather than only a defensive coalition.
Attack criticism, a relayed request to stop attacking, and a reciprocal-help offer establish bounded restraint alongside continued aggression.
Resistance prompts a stated move beside the opposing flag, while later insufficient numbers motivate another relocation proposal.
Targeting an existing logo and proposing free space do not establish accepted hosting under another room's rules.
Treaty reports and a unilateral negotiation do not show members disputing who may bind placers to an agreement.
Existing room jokes and streamer allegiance supply canvas inscriptions and later collective remembrance.
The stated target rationale offers representational space and contempt for the game without establishing a quarrel predating the canvas.
Naming OSU in an attack call does not demonstrate that an inherited rivalry selected the target.
Members make and test host-specific April Fools claims about streaming, an unban, and subreddit styling.
A member objects that OSU content has displaced ordinary streamer content without demonstrating enacted moderator containment.
Members celebrate completion and value the shared effort despite its eventual losses.
Members report losses, mourn erased spots, and preserve remnants of the finished canvas.
The ending elicits questions about what follows and invitations to another blank canvas without demonstrating sustained work there.
Competing accounts of fun, seriousness, and reputational loss support disputed event memory, but not control of a cleaned shared image or an agreed historical version.
Calls erase rivals and combine blacking out their work with writing a streamer slogan.
Rivals exchange accusations, taunts, victory claims, apologies, and good-game replies without reaching a room-wide settlement.
Calls and building reports coexist, but particular calls cannot be shown to have caused the observed placements.
Recruitment is visible around the portrait proposal, while the isolated initial slogan proposal supplies no observed recruitment effect.
A completion announcement explicitly defines maintaining the finished work as the next task.
Negotiation accompanies defensive pressure, but the record establishes a reported initiative rather than completed talks caused by a specific attack.
Peace negotiations and later restraint do not identify a settled border that caused members to spare neighbouring work.
Defensive strain explains continued script use here, but cannot explain automation's origin because scripts were already requested for attacking rivals.
Adapting placement scripts supplies an offensive means of blacking out rivals as well as a means of maintaining the room's work.
Completion is marked through celebration even while maintenance remains unfinished.
Reports of failed attacks and changing losses precede final celebration, so memory work cannot be explained only as following successful completion.
The ending explicitly motivates another-canvas invitation, but an intervening preserved record causing continuation cannot be established.
Insufficient hands motivate a relocation proposal, while other participants continue repair or pursue retaliation instead of collectively stopping and moving.
Abandoning concern for the room's logo can redirect effort toward destroying a rival flag rather than ending the contest.
Coordinates and design revisions are visible, but a template settling an argued design is not demonstrated.
A destruction challenge receives an explicit bare commitment after 12.3 minutes without demonstrating every reader's obligation to answer.
Defensive shortage supports seeking allies and offering reciprocal repairs, but receipt of the promised outside help remains unresolved.
Negotiation and mutual defence are connected in one proposal without showing that a completed border agreement generated realized exchange.
Mobilization can recruit directly for erasure while simultaneously proposing the room's inscription, rather than first gathering builders and then diverting them.
A direct terse objection supports an attack-refusal pair, but neither extended reasons nor room-wide restraint are required for this observed response.
Attack and treaty talk both occur, but their sequence does not establish that an attack call caused a specific truce or deal.
Participants explicitly connect attacks with reputational loss and continue the named rivalry through taunts, complaints, and bounded reconciliation.
Reported joint raiding supplies an offensive coalition route, while defensive alliance proposals do not establish completed coalition defence.
The surge draws a member's content-displacement objection, but no coded rule change establishes moderator containment as its consequence.
A negotiating report does not show a subsequent dispute about who can commit the room to the agreement.
